subject: Post-call: PayQuarry inference cost & pilot next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@payquarry.com>, Leo Martinez <leo@payquarry.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-14T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: PayQuarry inference cost & pilot next steps

Hi Julia / Leo —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap while it’s fresh and a proposed next steps list so we can size the pilot and get pricing aligned. If I missed anything, flag it and I’ll update.

Key pain & goals (as discussed)
- Current latency & cost blockers: your conversational assistant averages ~350 ms p99 but token spend is outpacing expected budget as usage scales (esp. nighttime spikes).
- Primary goal: improve response cost per user while keeping p95 latency <= 250 ms and preserving model quality for authorization/fraud dialogs.
- Constraints: procurement expects a predictable monthly spend cap (target $40–60k/mo for initial pilot); security review requires SOC2 evidence and VPC connectivity.

Technical levers we discussed
- Batching: expect 30–50% token-cost reduction for background (non-real-time) bulk inference (report generation, reconciliations) — savings depend on concurrency profile.
- KV/prefix caching: should cut repeated-context tokens by ~20–35% for your session flows (helpful for returning users and long sessions).
- Model variant routing: route low-sensitivity queries to smaller quantized variants during peak windows to control cost while keeping high-SLA traffic on the larger model.

Pilot outline & sizing assumptions (initial ask for confirmation)
- Duration: 8 weeks.
- Traffic profile for pilot: 1M tokens/day average (peak 3M), 60% chat-generative traffic, 40% embeddings/rl-related scoring.
- Expected unit-econ: with batching + caching we project a 45% reduction in per-token billing compared to naive per-request runs (detailed numbers in attached cost model).

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Julia: confirm the pilot traffic profile above (tokens/day, peak windows, critical latency SLO).
2) Leo / procurement: share any required PO language or contract deadlines if you need a committed capacity option vs hosted pay-as-you-go.
3) Redwood: we’ll produce a formal pilot cost model + SLA options (ben) and a short SOC2 evidence checklist (aditya) by EOD tomorrow.

Attachments: PayQuarry_pilot_scope_v1.pdf (pilot scope, acceptance criteria), pilot_cost_model.xlsx (ballpark TCO scenarios).

Thanks — happy to hop on another quick sync if that helps.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132
From: Julia Park <julia.park@payquarry.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Leo Martinez <leo@payquarry.com>, procurement@payquarry.com
Date: 2028-06-14T17:45:22-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: PayQuarry inference cost & pilot next steps

Marissa — thanks for the clear summary. This looks right at a high level. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Traffic confirmation: the 1M tokens/day is our conservative baseline; during business hours our product generates closer to 1.8M tokens/day and nightly batch jobs can push peaks near 3.2M. We can provide a traffic export for last 30 days to firm this up.

2) Latency SLO: p95 <= 250 ms is ideal for auth flows; for other dialogs p95 <= 500 ms is acceptable. We need clear rollback behavior if SLOs degrade.

3) Budget: procurement indicated we can earmark $50k/mo for the pilot, but cannot exceed $65k without additional approvals. We are open to a committed capacity pilot if Redwood can deliver predictable pricing and a fallback plan for model quality regressions.

Next: I’ll send the traffic export by EOD Friday. Please include in your formal cost model the committed vs hosted scenarios and a short runway estimate for each.

Julia
Julia Park
Head of ML, PayQuarry
julia.park@payquarry.com
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@payquarry.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-14T17:55:10-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: PayQuarry inference cost & pilot next steps

Thanks Julia — helpful numbers. Two quick notes on pricing levers and what I’ll include in the cost model:

- Committed capacity (dedicated pool) option: we can offer predictable monthly billing with a stepped discount at 3- and 6-month commits. For the 50k/mo target, the committed path reduces expected variable spend by ~25% vs hosted when utilization is >65%. It also removes per-token spikes from your billing profile.

- Hybrid routing: recommend routing auth-critical calls to a non-quantized variant on Dedicated with strict latency SLO; route conversational and batch traffic to a quantized variant or use automated downrouting during peak windows. That buys cost savings while preserving the SLOs you flagged.

I’ll attach a simple committed vs hosted comparison in the workbook (pilot_cost_model.xlsx) with break-evens at different utilization points.

—Ben
Ben Carter | Account Exec
ben_carter@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@payquarry.com>, Leo Martinez <leo@payquarry.com>

Date: 2028-06-15T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: PayQuarry inference cost & pilot next steps

Appreciate the quick reply, Julia. 

Plan of action we’ll take this week:
- Redwood deliverables (by 2028-06-16 EOD): updated pilot_cost_model.xlsx with committed vs hosted scenarios + sensitivity rows for batching/caching impact; a one-page SLA rollback policy; SOC2 evidence checklist and required connection details for VPC peering. (Ben + Aditya)
- PayQuarry deliverable (by 2028-06-18): traffic export for last 30 days and any procurement PO language you want pre-seeded.
- Quick follow-up: propose a 30-minute call next Wednesday (2028-06-21) to align on final pilot contract and kick scheduling. If that works for you, we’ll send a calendar invite.

Acceptance criteria for pilot (draft)
- Maintain p95 <= 250 ms for auth flows during >95% of business-hour windows, with an automated fallback to previous provider if degraded for >15 minutes.
- Realize >=30% unit-cost reduction vs current baseline when batching and caching are applied (measured over a 2-week rolling window).
- Production-like security posture: SOC2 evidence in place and VPC connectivity validated before data onboarding.

If those sound reasonable I’ll lock in the pilot doc and Ben will propose pricing bands in the workbook.

Thanks, and speak soon —
Marissa
(Attachments referenced as stubs): PayQuarry_pilot_scope_v1.pdf (application/pdf), pilot_cost_model.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
